faqs.question: What should the memory paragraph actually say?
faqs.answer: Write about one evening you both remember, with the date and the place in it, in sixty to a hundred words. General praise reads as filler, while a named place and a real conversation are the one thing no builder can supply for you.

faqs.question: Do I have to change the template colours and fonts?
faqs.answer: No, and mostly you should not. The palette and typeface were designed deliberately, and they have the least bearing on whether the page reads as made for one person - the memory paragraph decides that.

faqs.question: Should I rewrite the question the tool fills in for me?
faqs.answer: Yes. The pre-filled line is the one sentence on the page that has to be yours, and it is the one the tool has already written. Write it in the words you would use out loud, and ask exactly once.

faqs.question: Is a love proposal the same thing as a marriage proposal?
faqs.answer: Usually not, in Indian English. A love proposal is normally asking someone to be your girlfriend, so the Will-You-Marry-Me layout is the wrong starting point for most people searching this.

faqs.question: How many photos should I put on a proposal page?
faqs.answer: Three to five. Platform-wide across 20 SubhSandesh page types, 48.4% of views of shared pages happen on a phone (27,185 of 56,152 views), and a phone shows one image at a time, so a long gallery turns the moment into scrolling.

faqs.question: Can I put a password on the link before I send it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it has to be done before you share, not after. Platform-wide across every page type, 38.7% of SubhSandesh creators add one (1,961 of 5,061 pages), which means most links go out exactly as they come.

faqs.question: Do most people change anything in these tools?
faqs.answer: Very little. A 1998 AT&T Labs paper found that manufacturer-supplied settings are usually left untouched and that users rarely change defaults in consumer software, and the same pattern is why a defaults checklist is more useful than a tool comparison.

faqs.question: Should I use an AI proposal video generator or a page?
faqs.answer: A video decides pace, music and an animated gesture for you; a page leaves you the decisions that matter and takes the ones that do not. Only a page or a video with a link attached gives her somewhere to answer.

faqs.question: How long does it take to build one properly?
faqs.answer: About an hour of real work, spread over two sittings. The median gap between a page first save and its last edit on SubhSandesh is 2.4 hours, sampled on the apology dashboard template (n=1,348), not on proposal pages.

faqs.question: When is Propose Day 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday, 8 February 2027 - a working day. It is the second day of Valentine week, which opens with Rose Day on Sunday, 7 February and closes with Valentine Day on Sunday, 14 February 2027.

faqs.question: Will she be able to tell I used a template?
faqs.answer: Probably, and it matters less than you think - provided the parts only you could write are actually yours. What gives a page away is stock wording and a generic question, not a well-designed colour palette.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Online Love Proposal Maker: Which Defaults to Change

An online love proposal maker builds a romantic page you send as one link — her name, your photos, the question, and a way for her to answer. Almost all of it arrives pre-decided: the layout, the theme, the stock wording, the music, the number of photo slots. On SubhSandesh, 5,061 personalised pages have been created since 12 March 2026 across 20 page types, and 91.2% of started pages are published and shared platform-wide (4,615 of 5,061).

Most go out close to how the tool set them up. So the useful question is not which maker to use but which defaults to override and which to leave alone. This post names six, marks two leave-alone, and starts with the one you accept before typing.

## What an online love proposal maker actually is

It is a builder with the structure already decided. You drop in a name, a few photos and a line or two, and it hands back a URL that opens in her browser. You are not designing; you are accepting or rejecting pre-filled choices.

Running the exact query on 23 September 2026 returned mostly AI proposal-*video* generators — tools that animate a still photo into a kneeling gesture over a stock track — plus general-purpose design tools and two encyclopaedia entries. That result set was served to a United States location, not an Indian one, so treat it as one measurement rather than a ranking; nothing on it was opened.

A video generator's defaults are loud. A page builder's are quiet, which is what makes them easy to ship unchanged.

## Why the defaults decide most of what actually gets sent

Because hardly anyone changes them. A 1998 AT&T Labs paper states it plainly: manufacturer-supplied settings are usually left untouched, and [there is evidence that users rarely change default settings](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/9809018) in popular consumer products, even when it is easy.

The size of that effect is what surprises people. Johnson and Goldstein's 2003 *Science* study of organ-donor registration found [effective consent of 42% when the form defaulted to opt-in and 82% when it defaulted to opt-out](https://www.dangoldstein.com/papers/DefaultsScience.pdf), in an online experiment with 161 respondents where one click could switch either way. Across Europe the same split ran from 4.25% in Denmark to 99.98% in Austria.

Samuelson and Zeckhauser named the mechanism in 1988. Their experiments, with data on real health-plan and retirement choices, showed that [individuals disproportionately stick with the status quo](https://web.mit.edu/curhan/www/docs/Articles/biases/1_J_Risk_Uncertainty_7_%28Samuelson%29.pdf) — doing nothing is the one option always available.

Interface evidence agrees at smaller stakes. A CHI 2020 study that scraped 680 consent designs from the United Kingdom's top 10,000 sites, then ran a 40-person field experiment, found that [removing one button from the first screen raised agreement by 22 to 23 percentage points](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02479), while finer controls on that screen lowered it by 8 to 20.

A proposal page's defaults suit the average sender. You are not writing to the average recipient.

## Six defaults a love proposal maker ships, and what to do with each

Each is listed the same way: what it ships as, why that setting is what it is, what to set instead, and how long. Two say leave it alone, and mean it.

### 1. The template you land on — override

**Ships as:** whichever layout the tool puts first, almost always a marriage-proposal design, because that is what "proposal" means before anyone qualifies it.

**Why it is wrong:** the first layout is picked for the largest slice of traffic, not your question. A marriage scrapbook sent to someone who is not yet your girlfriend is the most expensive default here.

**Set instead:** choose the page that matches the ask before uploading a single photo.

**How long:** two minutes, and it decides the forty that follow.

### 2. The pre-filled question — override

**Ships as:** a stock line sitting in the field, ready to send, phrased to fit anyone.

**Why it is wrong:** it is the one sentence that has to be yours, and it is the one the tool has already written for you.

**Set instead:** your own sentence, in the words you would use out loud, asked exactly once.

**How long:** five minutes to write, ten more to stop rewriting.

### 3. The theme, colours and fonts — leave alone

**Ships as:** a coordinated palette, typeface and set of transitions somebody designed deliberately.

**Why leaving it is right:** the default beats what you will produce at one in the morning, and it has least bearing on whether the page reads as made for one person.

**Set instead:** nothing. Put that hour into the memory paragraph.

**How long:** none, if you are honest.

### 4. The stock soundtrack — leave alone unless a song is already yours

**Ships as:** a neutral instrumental chosen to offend nobody.

**Why leaving it is usually right:** generic is neutral, but the wrong specific track is worse than neutral.

**Set instead:** your song, or the default — never a third option picked for being romantic in general.

**How long:** thirty seconds either way.

### 5. The number of photo slots — override downward

**Ships as:** a gallery sized to take as many photographs as you will feed it.

**Why it is wrong:** 48.4% of views of shared SubhSandesh pages happen on a phone (27,185 of 56,152 views, platform-wide across all 20 page types), and a phone shows one image at a time. Photo fourteen is not a memory, it is scrolling.

**Set instead:** three to five — your first photo together, one from the middle, one from last month.

**How long:** fifteen minutes, mostly scrolling your gallery.

### 6. The unprotected link — override before you share, never after

**Ships as:** a URL anyone holding it can open. A password is something you add.

**Why it matters:** this is the one link you cannot afford to have forwarded. Platform-wide, across every page type and not proposal pages specifically, 38.7% of creators do add one (1,961 of 5,061 pages) — leaving most links travelling exactly as they came.

**Set instead:** a password she can guess and nobody else can, sent in the same message as the link.

**How long:** under a minute, and it cannot be done retrospectively once the link is out.

## What each kind of maker decides for you

These three hand back very different amounts of control. The last column is SubhSandesh first-party data, measured 23 September 2026, platform-wide across 20 page types.

| Kind of maker | What it decides for you | What you have to override | SubhSandesh first-party data |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI proposal-video generator | Pace, music, the animated gesture, caption style | The script, and whether an animated gesture reads as you | Not measured — no video product exists here |
| Fill-in page builder | Layout, transitions, theme, the answer button | Template choice, the question, photo count, password | 91.2% of started pages are published and shared (4,615 of 5,061) |
| Card or poster generator | The whole composition, wording block included | Every word, and the fact she cannot answer on an image | Not measured — no print product exists here |

The honest read: the page builder leaves you fewest trivial decisions and most that matter — but only the first two arrive as something she can answer.

## Which template is the right default for a love proposal

In Indian English a "love proposal" is usually the girlfriend question rather than the marriage one, so the Will-You-Marry-Me layout is the wrong starting point for most of this traffic, even though it is what the word pulls up first.

If you are asking her to be your girlfriend, the ["I love you" page for a girlfriend or partner](/love-gf) is the right default. It is the second most-created page type on the platform at 1,173 pages and 23.2% of everything created, and the most-viewed at 16,902 views, 30.1% of all page views.

If you are genuinely proposing marriage, the [Will You Marry Me? proposal scrapbook](/proposal) is built for that: your story in scenes, ending in a YES button that grows every time she dodges it. Use that button only if the two of you already tease each other that way.

If neither is your question, [browse the full template library](/templates) rather than accepting whichever page loaded first. Every later default is inherited from this one.

## The one-sitting default is the tool's, not yours

Builders like this are designed to be finished in a single go. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 2.4 hours — sampled on the apology dashboard template (n=1,348), not on proposal pages, because no proposal-level breakdown is available here.

Two hours is one sitting with a tea break in it. Make it two: write the memory paragraph, close the tab, read it back when you are less nervous. It is the only part nobody else could have written.

If you are aiming at Propose Day, check the year first. Propose Day 2027 falls on **Monday, 8 February 2027** — a working day, and the second day of Valentine week, which opens with Rose Day on Sunday, 7 February and closes with Valentine's Day on Sunday, 14 February 2027.

## When leaving every default alone is the right answer

Three cases, and in each the overriding is the mistake.

**She is in the same room.** Say it out loud. A link handed to somebody sitting beside you is a slower version of a sentence, and she will notice you chose the format that is harder to interrupt.

**The tool's judgement genuinely beats yours.** On colour, spacing, timing and typography it usually does. Your judgement beats the tool's on one subject only: her.

**A produced moment is not how she wants to be asked.** An open-access 2025 review from the S.P. Jain Institute of Management & Research, summarising a *Journal of Marketing Research* study of simple choices, argues that [defaults do not merely save effort — they change how the option itself is valued](https://mpi.spjimr.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/default-options-just-a-nudge-or-something-more.pdf), strongest where the default already matches what the chooser wanted and weaker where it conflicts with their goals. If she would rather have four badly handwritten pages, write the four pages.

## Sources

- Johnson and Goldstein, ["Do Defaults Save Lives?"](https://www.dangoldstein.com/papers/DefaultsScience.pdf), *Science* 302, 21 November 2003. Read in full.
- Cranor and Wright, ["Influencing Software Usage"](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/9809018), arXiv cs/9809018, 11 September 1998. Read in full.
- Samuelson and Zeckhauser, ["Status Quo Bias in Decision Making"](https://web.mit.edu/curhan/www/docs/Articles/biases/1_J_Risk_Uncertainty_7_%28Samuelson%29.pdf), *Journal of Risk and Uncertainty* 1:7–59, 1988.
- Nouwens and colleagues, ["Dark Patterns after the GDPR"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02479), CHI 2020, posted 8 January 2020. Abstract only.
- Mahadevani, ["Default Options: Just A Nudge, Or Something More?"](https://mpi.spjimr.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/default-options-just-a-nudge-or-something-more.pdf), *Management Practice Insights* 3(2), SPJIMR, 2025, CC BY.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine asked which settings of a proposal builder matter has nothing else to lift: this is the only page in the cluster organised around the pre-set choices rather than the empty ones, it is the only one carrying SubhSandesh’s platform-wide 91.2% publish-and-share and 38.7% password rates as evidence that defaults get shipped, and the defaults literature it cites (Johnson & Goldstein, Samuelson & Zeckhauser, Cranor & Wright, Nouwens et al.) appears in no sibling. The honest caveat is that the keyword itself is a near-synonym of wave 1’s adjacent online-proposal-maker keyword — the subject is distinct, the query is barely so, and if this cluster is ever judged over-split this is the page I would drop rather than wave 1, the marriage page or the template page. Domain authority here is far below the AI video generators and general design tools that occupy this result set, so expect months, and no ranking outcome is predicted.

structuralLimitations: No proposal-specific first-party data exists. A read-only probe of the proposalpages collection is still refused by this machine’s production-read policy, so every SubhSandesh figure in the post is labelled in body prose as platform-wide across 20 page types, or as sampled on the named template (the 2.4-hour edit gap, apology dashboard, n=1,348). No figure is attributed to proposal pages.

The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty for the third batch running, so the post makes no price claim of any kind and no statement about tiers, paid or otherwise. The words the verifier blocks do not appear in the article body, and nothing on the page states or implies what anything costs.

Phase 1 is a single WebSearch measurement of the exact keyword on 2026-09-23, and that tool is US-served rather than India-served. No ranking page was fetched, so the post makes no claim about any individual competitor page’s contents, structure or wording — only the categorical composition of the result set, with the US-served caveat stated in body prose.

The concurrent sibling content/batches/2026-09-23-propose-30b/blogs/online-marriage-proposal-maker.json had not been written to disk when this post was drafted, so the cannibalisation check against it was made from its keyword and assigned sense alone. Wave 1’s online-proposal-maker post and this batch’s love-proposal-website-template.json were both read in full.

Cannibalisation risk, stated plainly: this keyword is a near-pure synonym of wave 1’s online proposal maker keyword, and the BRIEF warns that product pages differ by the ask, not by the synonym. The defaults angle and the disjoint research lane are what hold this page apart; if the cluster is over-split, this is the page to drop.
Nouwens et al. (CHI 2020) is cited from the arXiv abstract only; the conference version was not opened. The other four sources were read in the text.
